reference.question: Find \((1,0)\cdot(0,1)\).
reference.solution:
Method 1: Perpendicular vectors

The coordinate basis vectors are perpendicular to each other, so their dot product is 0.

Method 2: Coordinate dot product

Multiplying corresponding coordinates and adding gives \((1,0)\cdot(0,1)=1\times0+0\times1=0\).

nodes.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram ; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.
nodes.label: 6.NS.C.6c

nodes.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).
nodes.label: 5.G.A.1

nodes.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.
nodes.label: 6.NS.C.6

nodes.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram . *Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
nodes.label: 3.NF.A.2

nodes.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.
nodes.label: 6.NS.C.6a

edges.reason: The additive stages of general four-operation signed expressions include signed sums and differences.
Primary column-row examples motivate ordered pairs; the later node reintroduces the same positional abstraction and order sensitivity directly.
edges.scope: prior experience locating by column and row

edges.reason: Perpendicular constructions and uniqueness explain orthogonal projections, but plotting on an existing square grid needs only its given axes. Keep the useful geometry preparation without imposing the full construction workflow.
Each coordinate axis is a number line with an origin, a direction and a unit. Plotting and reading coordinates is impossible without understanding those three elements of a number line.
edges.scope: coordinate axes as two perpendicular number lines

edges.reason: Each axis is a signed number line, so plotting signed coordinates uses number-to-position interpretation on it.
edges.scope: axes as number lines with negatives

edges.reason: A point's two coordinates form an ordered pair; swapping the entries generally changes the point.
Applying x1x2+y1y2 needs only the vectors' coordinates (h086), not componentwise addition or scaling. Linear combinations help derive the formula but are not needed to use it.
Modulus computation by Pythagoras is an explicit source criterion.
The zero-dot-product perpendicularity criterion explicitly uses dot products.
edges.scope: perpendicularity test via zero dot product
